items.title: `%pip` and `%uv` don't work in nushell if the path contains spaces
items.body:
Output of `python -c "import IPython; print(IPython.sys_info())"`:
```
{'commit_hash': '48ff029',
 'commit_source': 'installation',
 'default_encoding': 'utf-8',
 'ipython_path': '/Users/matteodelton/Downloads/Folder with '
                 'spaces/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/IPython',
 'ipython_version': '9.17.1',
 'os_name': 'posix',
 'platform': 'macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O',
 'sys_executable': '/Users/matteodelton/Downloads/Folder with '
                   'spaces/.venv/bin/python',
 'sys_platform': 'darwin',
 'sys_version': '3.14.8 (main, Oct  3 2026, 00:54:40) [Clang 22.1.3 ]'}
```

If the path of the notebook contains spaces, `%pip` and `%uv` magic commands don't work in [nushell](https://www.nushell.sh/). I guess this is due to differences in how escaping works since nushell is not a POSIX shell.

Here's a minimal reproducible example. When running `%pip install numpy`, I get
```
Error: nu::parser::parse_mismatch

  × Parse mismatch: expected operator.
   ╭─[source:1:69]
 1 │ '/Users/matteodelton/Downloads/Folder with spaces/.venv/bin/python' -m pip install numpy
   ·                                                                     ─┬
   ·                                                                      ╰── expected operator
   ╰────
  help: Check the syntax around this position — a typo, missing delimiter, or
        wrong separator is common.

Note: you may need to restart the kernel to use updated packages.
```

To run an external command in nushell, a caret (^) in front of the string is needed, as per the [documentation](https://www.nushell.sh/book/working_with_strings.html#strings-as-external-commands). However, I saw that `IPython/core/magics/packaging.py` is using `shlex.quote(s)`, and [`shlex`'s documentation ](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html#shlex.quote) says it's only designed for Unix shells, so the same problem might occur in other shells. One possible fix could be using functions that pass command arguments with lists such as [subprocess.run()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) with `shell=False`.

items.title: Self-referential ianvs dependency in requirements.txt breaks fresh installs (GovDoc2Poster, imagenet/multiedge_inference_bench)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

items.body:
**What happened**:
`pip install -r requirements.txt` fails immediately for two Ianvs examples because their `requirements.txt` lists `ianvs` itself as a pinned pip dependency:
- `examples/GovDoc2Poster/singletask_learning_bench/requirements.txt:5` → `ianvs>=0.1.0`
- `examples/imagenet/multiedge_inference_bench/requirements.txt:27` → `ianvs>=0.3.0`

`ianvs` is not published on PyPI (confirmed via `https://pypi.org/pypi/ianvs/json` → 404) — it's installed from source via `python setup.py install`, per the project's own Quick Start guide. Listing it as a version-pinned pip requirement causes the install to fail outright for any new user following the documented setup for either example.

**What you expected to happen**:
`pip install -r requirements.txt` should succeed for both examples, resolving only genuine third-party PyPI packages, since `ianvs` itself is installed separately via `python setup.py install` before any example's own requirements are installed.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
```bash
$ pip install "ianvs>=0.1.0"
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement ianvs>=0.1.0 (from versions: none)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for ianvs>=0.1.0
```
Same result running the full `pip install -r requirements.txt` against either of the two files listed above.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This is a repeated pattern across two independently-authored examples, not a one-off typo — likely a templated or copy-pasted requirements header that assumed `ianvs` was pip-installable. I checked related open issues (#132, #514, #535) and found none reporting this specific self-referential dependency pattern.

Note: `sedna>=0.1.0` in the GovDoc2Poster file is fine and should stay — Sedna is genuinely published on PyPI, unlike Ianvs.

Fix is a one-line deletion in each file:

```diff
--- a/examples/GovDoc2Poster/singletask_learning_bench/requirements.txt
+++ b/examples/GovDoc2Poster/singletask_learning_bench/requirements.txt
@@ -2,7 +2,6 @@
 # 新版政府代理依赖包

 # Core dependencies
-ianvs>=0.1.0
 sedna>=0.1.0

 # Document processing (轻量级方案)
```

```diff
--- a/examples/imagenet/multiedge_inference_bench/requirements.txt
+++ b/examples/imagenet/multiedge_inference_bench/requirements.txt
@@ -24,7 +24,6 @@ h11==0.14.0
 h5py==3.8.0
 huggingface-hub==0.16.4
 humanfriendly==10.0
-ianvs>=0.3.0
 idna==3.7
 imageio==2.31.2
 importlib-metadata==6.7.0
```

I'm happy to open a PR with this fix if it's welcome.

items.title: [Fix] v0.3.1 — Correctness fixes across source, docs, and infrastructure

milestone.title: v0.3.1
milestone.description:
Correctness fixes found during v0.3.0 code review — no new features, no API changes.

**Runtime Issues:**
1. `peek()` / `build_dict()` shallow copy → deepcopy
2. `ConfigBuilder` missing `super().__init__()`
3. `DataClassConfigBuilder` missing `super().__init__()`
4. Loaders re-wrap `ConfigNotFoundError` as `ConfigLoadError`

**Output & Coercion Issues:**
5. TOML error message references wrong package name
6. `DataClassConfigBuilder` bool coercion missing `"on"` / `"off"`
7. `_instantiate_dataclass` inconsistent type guard

**Docs Issues:**
8. `exceptions.py` module docstring wrong package name
9. `_check_file_exists` docstring wrong exception type
10. `RawConfigBuilder` docstring typo (`Schmea-less`)

**Infrastructure Issues:**
11. `typing_extensions` not declared as explicit dependency
12. `actions/checkout@v5` → `@v6` in two workflows
13. Missing `tests/unit/__init__.py`
14. `pyproject.toml` include pattern too broad (`pyconfig*` → `pyconfigre*`)

items.body:
# Summary

v0.3.0 code review uncovered 14 correctness, documentation, and infrastructure issues. This umbrella issue tracks all fixes for the v0.3.1 patch release — no new features, no API changes.

The issues span four areas: runtime bugs in the builder pipeline and loaders, incorrect output and coercion behaviour, docstring/documentation inaccuracies, and project infrastructure gaps. They are organised into four sub-issues that can be worked in parallel.

---

# What to Change

## Runtime / source code bugs

**Problem:**
  - `peek()` and `build_dict()` use `dict(self._data)` which is a **shallow copy** — mutating nested values in the returned dict silently corrupts the builder's internal state. The existing test `test_peek_is_nondestructive` only checks top-level mutation, not nested mutation.
  - `ConfigBuilder.__init__` and `DataClassConfigBuilder.__init__` both set `self._data = {}` directly instead of calling `super().__init__()`. If `RawConfigBuilder.__init__` changes in the future, the subclasses will silently diverge.
  - In `json.py`, `yaml.py`, and `toml.py`, the pattern `except ConfigLoadError: raise` does not catch `ConfigNotFoundError` (a sibling, not subclass of `ConfigLoadError`). The `ConfigNotFoundError` from `_check_file_exists()` falls through to `except Exception` and gets re-wrapped as `ConfigLoadError`, losing the original exception type.

**Expected behaviour:**
  - `peek()` and `build_dict()` return deep copies — mutating nested dicts in the result must not affect the builder
  - `ConfigBuilder` and `DataClassConfigBuilder` call `super().__init__()` to properly initialise the parent class
  - `ConfigNotFoundError` propagates through file loaders without being re-wrapped as `ConfigLoadError`

## Output & coercion inconsistencies

**Problem:**
  - `loaders/toml.py:59` references the wrong package name: `pip install pyconfig[toml]` instead of `pip install pyconfigre[toml]`. Users on Python < 3.11 without `tomli` see a misleading install instruction.
  - `ENVLoader._parse_value` recognises `"on"` and `"off"` as boolean values, but `dataclass_builder._coerce_value` does not (`_TRUTHY` and `_FALSY` sets omit them). This creates an inconsistency: `MY_DEBUG=on` via env → `True`, but `debug: "on"` from YAML through `DataClassConfigBuilder` → no coercion, passed through as the string `"on"`.
  - `_instantiate_dataclass` line 315 uses `isinstance(field_type, type)` while lines 310–312 use `_is_concrete_type(field_type)`. On Python 3.10, parameterized generics like `list[str]` pass `isinstance(type)` but fail `_is_concrete_type()`. Not a runtime crash (because `_coerce_value` has its own guard), but inconsistent and fragile.

**Expected behaviour:**
  - TOML error message says `pip install pyconfigre[toml]`
  - `_coerce_value` recognises `"on"` and `"off"` for bool coercion, matching `ENVLoader`
  - `_instantiate_dataclass` uses `_is_concrete_type()` consistently on all code paths

## Documentation & docstring inaccuracies

**Problem:**
  - `exceptions.py:1` module docstring says `"""Exception classes for pyconfig."""` — wrong package name, should be `pyconfigre`
  - `loaders/base.py:88` — the `_check_file_exists` docstring Raises section says `ConfigLoadError`, but the method actually raises `ConfigNotFoundError`
  - `builder/raw_builder.py:36` — docstring example heading says `Schmea-less usage::` instead of `Schema-less usage::`

**Expected behaviour:**
  - All docstrings reference the correct package name, exception type, and spelling

## Infrastructure & project configuration gaps

**Problem:**
  - `raw_builder.py` imports `from typing_extensions import Self`, but `typing_extensions` is not declared in `pyproject.toml` dependencies. It works today because Pydantic pulls it in transitively — but when Pydantic becomes optional in v0.4.0, `RawConfigBuilder` and `DataClassConfigBuilder` will break on import.
  - `pr-lifecycle.yml` (lines 50, 91) and `sync-labels.yml` (line 36) use `actions/checkout@v5` while all other workflows use `@v6`
  - Every test directory has an `__init__.py` (`tests/`, `tests/integration/`, `tests/unit/builder/`, `tests/unit/loaders/`) except `tests/unit/` — inconsistent and can cause issues with some test discovery configurations
  - `pyproject.toml` `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` has `include = ["pyconfig*"]` which is unnecessarily broad. Should be `["pyconfigre*"]` for specificity.
  - `CHANGELOG.md` v0.2.0 section has three cosmetic typos: `RawConfigbuilder` → `RawConfigBuilder`, `this is the terminal` → `This is the terminal`, `fprward reference` → `forward reference`

**Expected behaviour:**
  - `typing_extensions>=4.0` declared as an explicit dependency
  - All workflows use `actions/checkout@v6`
  - `tests/unit/__init__.py` exists
  - Setuptools include pattern matches only `pyconfigre*`
  - CHANGELOG typos corrected

---

# Scope of Changes

Pure correctness patch touching source code (`builder/`, `loaders/`), documentation (`exceptions.py`, `CHANGELOG.md`), project configuration (`pyproject.toml`), CI workflows, and test infrastructure.

---

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 14 issues listed above are implemented
- [ ] Regression tests added for: nested-dict mutation through `peek()`, `"on"` / `"off"` bool coercion, `ConfigNotFoundError` propagation through loaders

items.body:
## Describe the bug

One `apm install` command cannot reliably add packages from GitHub Enterprise Server and GitHub.com.

I expect this host-qualified form to work without a prior manifest edit:

```bash
apm install --global \
  'github.corp.example.com/acme/internal-skills/.agents/skills/jdk-installer' \
  'github.com/example/android-skills/performance/analyzer' \
  'github.com/example/kotlin-skills/skills/java-to-kotlin'
```

This is the normal package-manager workflow: name the packages in one install command, then let APM update the manifest and lockfile. It also matches the README promise to [install from GitHub Enterprise and any Git host](https://github.com/microsoft/apm#1-portable-by-manifest).

## Current behavior

APM 0.29.0 fails in two ways:

1. Without `GITHUB_HOST`, APM does not recognize the custom hostname as GHES. It treats the remaining repository and skill path as one repository path.
2. With `GITHUB_HOST=github.corp.example.com`, validation recognizes all explicit hosts. The download phase can still route the `github.com` packages through the GHES host.

The first case reports that the custom hostname "was treated as a single repository path" because it was not recognized. The second case tells the user to supply the full `github.com` hostname even though the original argument already supplied it.

The second case attempts clone URLs equivalent to:

```text
https://github.corp.example.com/example/android-skills.git
https://github.corp.example.com/example/kotlin-skills.git
```

The install fails and restores the previous `apm.yml`.

## Expected behavior

Each host-qualified argument must keep its own host through the complete install pipeline.

The example command must:

- Resolve the internal package from its specified GHES host.
- Resolve the public packages from `github.com`.
- Detect each repository boundary and preserve its skill subpath.
- Add equivalent object entries to the global `apm.yml`.
- Pin each resolved commit in `apm.lock.yaml`.
- Use the normal configured or detected targets.

An explicit hostname must take precedence over `GITHUB_HOST`. That variable must apply only to shorthand arguments without a hostname.

Host identity is also a credential boundary. APM must never send GitHub.com credentials to GHES or GHES credentials to GitHub.com.

## Current workaround

Manually add explicit `git:`, `path:`, and `ref:` objects to `~/.apm/apm.yml`. Then run:

```bash
GITHUB_HOST=github.corp.example.com apm install --global
```

I validated this workaround with APM 0.29.0. Install, uninstall, reinstall, and frozen reinstall all succeeded.

## Suggested implementation direction

Normalize each host-qualified positional argument to the existing object model before APM writes and rereads manifest state. Reuse the existing object parser and manifest-driven download path.

The fix should not add a new command, manifest schema, or structured CLI syntax.

Relevant code paths include:

- `src/apm_cli/commands/install.py`: positional package resolution and manifest updates.
- `src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py`: explicit hosts, repository boundaries, paths, and object parsing.
- `src/apm_cli/deps/download_strategies.py`: explicit dependency host versus `GITHUB_HOST` fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- The example command succeeds without `GITHUB_HOST`, `--https`, or a prior manifest edit.
- One command installs multiple subpath packages from GHES and GitHub.com.
- Explicit hosts survive validation, persistence, authentication, download, locking, update, and uninstall.
- `#<sha>`, `#<branch>`, and `#<tag>` refs continue to work.
- The manifest records the correct `git`, `path`, and `ref` for each package.
- The lockfile records the correct host, virtual path, and resolved commit.
- Credentials remain isolated by host.
- Existing shorthand and `GITHUB_HOST` behavior remains compatible.
- Failure remains transactional.
- Tests cover both failure modes and a successful mixed-host install.
- The CLI dependency documentation includes one mixed-host example.

## Related issues

- [#1970](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/1970) covers complete GitHub `SKILL.md` URLs, not mixed hosts.
- [#872](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/872) covers monorepo subpaths and the manifest workaround. It is closed.
- [#1013](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/1013) covered direct HTTPS credentials. It is closed.
- [#2066](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2066) covered GitLab subpath shorthand. It is closed.

As of 2026-09-02, I found no open issue in the tracker that covers this exact case.

## Environment

- APM: 0.29.0
- Scope: global user scope
- Targets: `agent-skills`, `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, and `cursor`

items.title: Issues to be addressed
items.body:
Critical — the library doesn't work as-is

1.  import QudLy  fails (verified).  __init__.py  line 4 imports  apply_gate_2 , which doesn't exist anywhere — it was commented out in  ausiliary.py  but the import was never removed. Nothing in the package is usable until this is fixed.
2. Floating-point  int(math.log(...))  bug (verified:  int(math.log(3**5, 3))  →  4 , not  5 ). This pattern appears in  apply_gate ,  apply_QFT ,  measure_single ,  measure_prob_single , and  indexes . For 5 qutrits (and other sizes where the float log lands just below the integer), the qudit count is computed wrong →  reshape  crashes or silently produces garbage. Fix: compute  num  with exact integer arithmetic.

Correctness bugs (verified by analysis)

3.  apply_QFT  phase formula is wrong:  theta = np.pi * 2**(config.DIM*(k-i)) . The qudit QFT needs controlled-ω phases, i.e.  theta = π  (base matrix  P(π) = Z ). The current formula is wrong for every dimension — even for qubits it yields  π/4  where the QFT requires  π  (a controlled-Z).
4.  apply_CX  is wrong for d > 2: it applies the Fourier  F  on both sides of CZ ( F·CZ·F ), but the correct decomposition is  F·CZ·F† . Since  F Z F = X†  (not  X ), the result is  Σ|i⟩⟨i| ⊗ X⁻ⁱ  — the inverse SUMX. It only works for qubits because  X = X†  there.  apply_SWAP  (built from 3×  apply_CX ) inherits this bug.
5.  Gate_H  is misnamed: its matrix is  ω^(-(i)k)/√d  = the inverse Fourier ( H† ), not the standard qudit Hadamard.  apply_QFT  silently compensates with  .dagger() , which makes the code confusing and fragile.

Design / robustness issues

6.  Gate  uses  @abstractmethod  but isn't an  ABC  — the decorator is a no-op;  Matrix()  is never enforced.
7.  State  requires an  N  identifier that is stored but never used — pure friction for the user.
8.  Total_state  has no normalization or validation, while  measure / measure_single  call  np.random.choice(p=prob)  — an unnormalized total state raises  ValueError  (probabilities must sum to 1).
9.  decompose()  is a memory bomb: it allocates  np.eye(self.dim) , and for a  Total_state   dim = dⁿ  — a 10-qudit state allocates a 59049×59049 matrix just to print amplitudes.
10. Global mutable  DIM :  set_dim()  has no validation and silently invalidates every gate/state created earlier.
11. Controlled gates build a  d²×d²  block-diagonal  matrix  that is never used —  apply_gate  only uses  base_matrix . Wasted computation and a misleading API.
12. Fragile exact float comparisons:  theta == np.pi  (in  Gate_SUMP ),  prob[l] != 0  (in  measure_prob* ).
13.  self.parameters = (theta)  is a float, not the tuple the base class declares.

Project hygiene

14. No packaging — no  pyproject.toml / setup.py , so it can't be  pip install ed.
15. No tests, no CI — given bugs #2–#4, a small test suite (e.g., "QFT of |0…0⟩ is uniform", "CX|10⟩=|11⟩") would have caught everything.
16. README is one line; no usage examples or API docs.
17. Module name typo:  ausiliary.py  (should be  auxiliary.py ).
18. Dead code: the large commented-out  apply_gate_2  block in  ausiliary.py , the  #CASINO  comment in  apply_gate , and unused imports ( Au ,  is_controlled_by ).

items.body:
An onboarding-readiness audit of `src/content/docs/oss/**` against `Giskard-AI/giskard-oss@main` (`giskard-checks 1.0.2rc1`, `giskard-scan 1.0.0rc1`), optimized for a developer who has never used Giskard and wants a first check running in 10 minutes.

Every claim below was verified by reading the library source or executing against it.

## The five things that most hurt a new developer

1. **The checks quickstart cannot run, and never says why.** It configures `Generator(model="openai/gpt-5.4-nano")` — a model that appears nowhere in giskard-oss (the library default is `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `libs/giskard-checks/src/giskard/checks/settings.py:10`). The setup cells are stripped from the rendered page, so the reader never learns an API key is needed; the first visible cell dies with `WorkflowError: Step processing failed`.
2. **Five install variants across the tree, two of them broken.** `oss/solutions/scan-vulnerabilities.mdx` omitted `--pre`, so it installed Giskard **2.19.2** and every sample on the page failed. The notebooks used `pip install giskard-checks`, which has no candidate because everything shipped is a pre-release.
3. **Documented API that does not exist.** `how-to/simulate-users.ipynb` built a whole section on a `simulator_output` metadata key with zero occurrences in giskard-oss — the notebook's own recorded output proves the branch never fired. Also a phantom `Persona` class, a phantom `Equals(key=...)` parameter, and a phantom `answer_key`.
4. **`Suite` was documented nowhere in how-to or use-cases**, so four pages hand-rolled ~400 lines reimplementing it, including a 134-line `RAGTestSuite`. The CI/CD guide shipped no CI report despite `SuiteResult.to_junit_xml` existing.
5. **No single golden path, and no failure ever shown.** Four peer sidebar groups offered four plausible starts, three pages nominated three different first destinations, and `/oss` linked neither Scan nor Solutions. Every recorded output across 13 notebooks was a pass, and no page documented a single error message.

## Also found

- The execution model in `explanation/core-concepts.md` was wrong in three ways: checks run per **step** (not per interaction), a spec is an async generator that can yield many interactions, and a failing step marks every later step SKIP.
- `MISSING` vs `None` was documented backwards across every static-value field in the checks reference. Passing `None` is a value and silently disables the `*_key` fallback.
- The scan install page pointed LiteLLM users at `GiskardLLMGenerator`, which raises `ValueError: Provider 'mistral' is not configured and not in the registry` mid-scan. LiteLLM needs `LiteLLMGenerator`.
- 10 public symbols in `giskard.checks.__all__` were documented nowhere; `Scenario` was missing six of its eleven builder methods, including `with_target()`.
- No troubleshooting page, no migration page, no versioning/stability policy, no security or issue-reporting path, and no cost or latency figure on either golden path.
- `scan/how-to/index.mdx` omitted three of its eight pages, including `wrap-your-agent` — the step between the toy tutorial and a real agent.

## Not a problem

The mechanical API delta is clean: `scripts/snapshot-api.py` + `scripts/diff-api.py` against `docs/api-baseline/` show zero real deltas for both packages. Nothing documented has been removed or re-signed. (The 74 raw deltas were `X | Y` vs `Union[X, Y]` interpreter noise — fixed separately so the differ stops crying wolf.)

The scan reference and explanation pages were checked symbol by symbol and contained no wrong signature, default, tag, or constant.

Full report with every finding as `file:line — problem — fix`, and a worklist of 52 PR-sized items ranked P0/P1/P2, is attached to the PR.

items.title: Modernize the Dockerfile for reproducible, supported builds

labels.name: infrastructure
labels.description: Docker and CI/CD setup and/or configuration

items.body:
## Summary

Modernize the **`Dockerfile`** so it builds deterministically, uses a
supported base image, and matches the project's current dependency and
workflow reality (no more deadsnakes/poetry-era workarounds if the project
moves to `uv`).

## What is the issue?

The current `Dockerfile` has several problems:

1. `FROM ubuntu` — **no tag**, so builds are not reproducible (base image
   contents change over time).
2. It installs Python via the **deadsnakes PPA** and then registers
   `python3.10`/`python3.11` with `update-alternatives`, referencing a
   `python3.10` that is never installed in the `RUN` step
   (`update-alternatives --install ... /usr/bin/python3.10 1` will create a
   broken alternative).
3. `CMD cd root \ && mkdir src` combined with
   `ENTRYPOINT export PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH" && cd root/src && /bin/bash`
   is fragile and depends on shell form behavior; there is no `WORKDIR`, and
   the directory layout (`/root/src`) is hard-coded.
4. It installs a large set of system packages (`portaudio19-dev`,
   `libpcap-dev`, `libgmp-dev`, `gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu`, etc.) that are likely
   leftover from older builds (e.g., when `pysqlite3` still needed compiling —
   see closed issues #38/#39/#42/#46); many are no longer needed.
5. The README's Docker instructions tell users to run `poetry install`
   *inside* the container after building, which duplicates dependency
   installation and contradicts the "container includes everything" model.

## How can you tell it is a problem?

- `docker build -t chasten .` produces a very large image and takes a long
  time (installs many unused packages).
- The image is not reproducible: rebuilding later pulls a different `ubuntu`
  base and possibly different PPA package versions.
- The `update-alternatives` command with the non-existent `python3.10` links
  can leave `python3` pointing at the wrong interpreter inside the image.

## How to replicate (automated or manual)

1. Run `docker build -t chasten .` and time it; note the installed packages
   that are irrelevant to `chasten`'s runtime (e.g., `portaudio19-dev`).
2. Run the container as the README describes and then `python3 --version`
   and `chasten --help` inside it; observe whether the image actually has
   the tool installed or whether you must still `poetry install` by hand.

## Preliminary ideas for the fix

1. Use a pinned base image, e.g.:

   ```dockerfile
   FROM python:3.11-slim-bookworm   # or 3.12 with a digest pin
   ```

2. Install the OS packages that are genuinely needed by
   `chasten`'s dependencies (check what the current dependency set needs;
   `libsqlite3-dev` may still be required for `sqlite-utils`/`sqlean-py`).
3. Adopt the project's package manager of the future (see the Poetry→uv
   issue): if the project moves to `uv`, use the official
   `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` image stage or install `uv` and run
   `uv sync --frozen` inside the build.
4. Use `WORKDIR /workspace` (or similar), `COPY . .`, install dependencies,
   and run the test suite during the build (`RUN uv run task test`) so the
   image doubles as a CI-consistent environment.
5. If you must support `poetry` during the transition, install Poetry with
   `pipx`/`pip` and `poetry install --no-interaction` in the build instead
   of in the README instructions.
6. Update the README Docker section to match the new build and run commands
   (no manual in-container `poetry install`).

## How to confirm the fix works

- `docker build` completes in a reasonable time from a clean cache and
  produces a reproducible image (rebuild with the same base digest yields the
  same behavior).
- `docker run --rm chasten chasten --help` works without extra steps.
- The test suite (`task test`/`uv run task test`) passes inside the
  container.
- `docker image ls` shows a significantly smaller image than the current
  one.

## Codebase details / context

- `Dockerfile` (root of the repository) — currently `FROM ubuntu` with
  deadsnakes-based Python 3.11 setup, `curl -sSl` (typo for `-sSL`) pip
  bootstrap, and the fragile `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` pair.
- `README.md` — the "🐋 Docker" section describes the old workflow.
- Related history: closed issues #38, #39, #40, #42, #44, #46 (installation
  pain points, several caused by `pysqlite3` needing a compiler; the
  dependency set changed since, so the Dockerfile's compiler/portaudio
  packages are likely stale).

items.title: Rename repo to smart-social-contracts/realms-gos before the Realms GOS announcement
items.body:
## Summary

Rename this repository from `smart-social-contracts/realms` to `smart-social-contracts/realms-gos` **before Realms GOS is publicly announced**.

Everything public already uses `realms-gos`: the PyPI package (`pip install realms-gos`), the GaaS implementation id (`gos_implementation = "realms-gos"`), and the product name "Realms GOS". The repo slug is the only one that differs. Once an announcement, forum post or docs site publishes the URL, it is much harder to change.

Checked on 2026-10-04: `smart-social-contracts/realms-gos` does not exist yet, so the name is free.

## Scope

Source and repositories only.

**Renamed:** the GitHub repo slug, plus every source reference to `smart-social-contracts/realms` (and the typo `smartsocialcontracts/realms`).

**Not renamed:**

- CLI command `realms` (`pip install realms-gos`, then `realms …`)
- PyPI package `realms-gos` (already correct)
- Python package `realms`, canister names (`realm_backend`, `realm_frontend`, …)
- Sibling repos: `realms-extensions`, `realms-codices`, `realms-billing`, `realms-strategy`
- npm scope `@realmsgos/*`

## Redirects

After a rename, GitHub permanently redirects web URLs, `git clone/fetch/push`, the API, release downloads and `raw.githubusercontent.com` from the old slug to the new one. **The redirect ends if anyone ever creates a new repo named `realms` in this org.** Don't do that.

Two source spots must still be edited, because a redirect is not enough:

- **`fleet_registry.py`.** `FLEET_REGISTRIES_URL` is fetched with an IC HTTP outcall, which does not follow redirects and accepts only HTTP 200. Point it straight at `raw.githubusercontent.com/smart-social-contracts/realms-gos/...`. No fallback URL.
- **npm `repository.url`.** `publish-extension-packages.yml` runs `npm publish --provenance`. npm rejects the publish when `package.json` `repository.url` does not match the repo that built it. Update the three packages under `packages/` to the new slug before the next publish.

These keep working via the redirect, and still get updated so the source names the real repo:

- Casals `release:smart-social-contracts/realms@…` pins (downloaded with Python `urllib`, which follows redirects)
- PyPI upload in `release.yml` (twine + `PYPI_API_TOKEN`, not a trusted publisher bound to the repo name)
- Browser fetches of `fleet-tokens.json` and codex branding
- No workflow uses `uses: smart-social-contracts/realms/...`
- GitHub Pages is not enabled on this repo

## Order

The new slug 404s until the rename. Update source **after** the rename, in the same window:

1. Rename the repo.
2. Merge the reference updates (this repo, submodules, other repos).
3. Confirm the search below is clean and CI is green.

## Checklist

### 1. Rename

- [ ] GitHub → Settings → Repository name → `realms-gos`
- [ ] `curl -sI https://github.com/smart-social-contracts/realms` returns `301` to `realms-gos`

items.title: Add JSON Schema validation for Sentinel policy YAML
items.body:
## Problem

`load_policy()` in `scripts/gsh-sentinel-deploy.py` (line ~127) parses `configs/sentinel-policy-default.yaml` with plain `yaml.safe_load` and no schema validation. A malformed or incomplete policy file (typo'd key, wrong type, missing threshold) silently falls back to `DEFAULT_POLICY` or fails deep inside a hunt's threshold logic instead of failing fast with a clear message.

## Expected files

- `schemas/sentinel-policy.schema.json` - JSON Schema describing the policy structure (global, sentinel, hunt_001–hunt_004, ztlv sections as seen in `configs/sentinel-policy-default.yaml`).
- Update `load_policy()` in `scripts/gsh-sentinel-deploy.py` to validate against the schema (e.g. via `jsonschema`, added as an optional dependency in `requirements.txt` with a stdlib fallback that does basic key/type checks if `jsonschema` isn't installed, consistent with this repo's "stdlib fallback" pattern).
- A `gsh policy validate <path>` style helper (can be a small function/CLI flag on the existing script; a full `gsh` CLI package is out of scope for this issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- Loading `configs/sentinel-policy-default.yaml` passes validation with no warnings.
- Loading a policy file missing a required key, or with a threshold field set to the wrong type (e.g. a string where a number is expected), fails with a specific error message naming the field and the file, not a generic exception or silent fallback.
- Works with `jsonschema` uninstalled (stdlib fallback) and installed.

## Example

```
$ python scripts/gsh-sentinel-deploy.py --policy configs/bad-policy.yaml --target x --mode passive
ERROR: Invalid policy 'configs/bad-policy.yaml': hunt_001.loop_threshold must be a number, got str
```

## Test requirements

- Unit test with a valid policy file (should pass).
- Unit test with 2-3 invalid policy files (missing key, wrong type, unknown top-level section) asserting the specific error raised.

---

## Contributor guide

- **Difficulty:** Intermediate, about 3 to 5 hours
- **Files likely involved:** `schemas/sentinel-policy.schema.json` (new), `scripts/gsh-sentinel-deploy.py` (`load_policy()`, line ~127), `configs/sentinel-policy-default.yaml` (read-only reference), `tests/test_policy_validation.py` (new)
- **Tip:** Start with the default policy YAML: the schema must accept it unchanged. Then write the bad-policy tests first.

**Run the tests locally**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/gsh-framework.git && cd gsh-framework
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/ -v      # full suite, currently 116 tests
ruff check .                    # lint, enforced in CI
```

**To claim this:** comment "I'll take this" and open a PR whenever you are ready; a draft PR early is fine. If you get stuck, ask on this thread and the maintainer will point you in the right direction. Small design questions are cheaper to ask before you write the code than after.

We came across this issue over at the `shap` repo, trying to run tests with the latest versions of both pytorch and lightgbm. We initially raised this issue on the pytorch issue tracker: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/121101 .

However, the underlying issue doesn't seem to be specific just to pytorch or lightgbm, but rather it relates to the _mutual compatibility_ of pytorch and lightgbm. The issue seems to relate to multiple ~OpenML~ OpenMP runtimes being loaded.

So, I thought it would be worth raising the issue here too in the hope that it helps us collectively find a fix.

items.title: Lazy __getattr__ public-API façade: worth an ADR sanctioning it plus a TYPE_CHECKING block
items.body:
## What I noticed

`views_r2darts2/__init__.py:45-77` (and `dataset/__init__.py:43`) expose the public API through a PEP-562 lazy `__getattr__`: each name in `__all__` is imported on first access rather than at package import.

The reason is a good one, and it's stated in `pyproject.toml:21-25`: `views-pipeline-core` is an optional `manager` extra, so eager imports would make `import views_r2darts2` fail for anyone who didn't install it. The façade also keeps `torch`/`darts` off the import path until a class is actually used. Nice engineering.

It's also 33 lines of import logic in an `__init__.py`, which the package's structural convention describes as "ghost logic" and asks contributors to avoid. So the rule and the code disagree — and I think both are right, which is exactly why it's worth writing down.

## Why I think it's worth a decision

**Both sides are defensible, so the disagreement will recur.** Someone will read the rule, "fix" the façade with eager imports, and break every environment that skipped the `manager` extra. Or someone will read the façade, conclude logic in `__init__` is fine here, and put something less benign in the next one. Neither person would be wrong given what's currently written. The fix is a paragraph saying which wins and why.

**The façade has a few real costs that are easy to mitigate once acknowledged.**
- *Errors surface in a surprising place.* `from views_r2darts2 import DartsForecastingModelManager` succeeds even without `views-pipeline-core`; the `ImportError` fires later, on first use, from inside `__getattr__`, pointing at `__init__.py` rather than the missing dependency. A newcomer's first encounter with the problem is a confusing traceback.
- *Tooling can't see the names.* Static analysers, IDE completion and type checkers can't resolve names that only exist through `__getattr__`. `__all__` promises eleven; a linter sees none defined. The standard fix — an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block mirroring the imports — isn't there yet.
- *Typos degrade.* A misspelt name raises `AttributeError` at use time rather than `ImportError` at import.

None of these is a reason to remove the façade. All of them are the kind of thing a short ADR states so nobody is surprised.

## What a fix could look like

**Recommended: keep it, sanction it, add the mitigations.**
- A short ADR ("Lazy public-API façade"): why (optional extra; import-time cost), scope (exactly these two `__init__.py` files, nowhere else), mitigations.
- An `if TYPE_CHECKING:` import block so tooling resolves every `__all__` name.
- Wrap the manager's deferred import so a missing `views-pipeline-core` produces an error that names the extra to install.
- One line in the structural convention pointing at the ADR as its sanctioned exception.

**Alternative:** eager imports, drop the optional extra. Simpler, but a cost for every downstream that doesn't need the manager.

## How we'd know it's done

- The rule and the code agree, in writing.
- `TYPE_CHECKING` block present; static tools resolve all `__all__` names.
- Missing `manager` extra yields a message like `pip install "views-r2darts2[manager]"`.

Detailed Summarization --- ## Issue [#132](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/132) - Unclear dependencies for Ianvs **Category:** Ecosystem / Installation Blocker - affects ALL examples ### Introduction Issue #132 documents the architectural root cause of Ianvs's dependency crisis: Sedna is distributed as an offline wheel with pinned `~=` version constraints, creating irreconcilable conflicts with newer packages. The `colorlog` missing crash (Bug 8) and the PyPI Sedna name collision (Bugs 9/10) are downstream manifestations of this same architectural gap, and CI has been silently passing with the wrong Sedna installed (PR #417 finding), making these the hardest class of bugs to detect in the entire project. ## Challenge ### **Bug 8 - `colorlog` missing from core `requirements.txt`** Ianvs fails before any example code executes: ``` File "core/common/log.py", line 18, in import colorlog ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'colorlog' ``` > --- ### **Bug 9 - `pip install sedna` installs wrong PyPI package (name collision)** The installed package exposes modules for unit conversion, not KubeEdge: ```python >>> import pkgutil, sedna >>> [m.name for m in pkgutil.iter_modules(sedna.__path__)] ['convert', 'maths', 'physics', 'prime', 'system', 'voice'] # AttributeError: module 'sedna' has no attribute '__version__' ``` > This collision is completely invisible. The contributor gets `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sedna.datasources'` with no indication the wrong package is installed. The contributor's first instinct is to reinstall sedna, which reinstalls the wrong package again. > **The CI connection that nobody else has made explicit:** PR #417 reveals that the CI workflow was installing Sedna from a path that does not exist (`${{github.workspace}}/resources/third_party/*` instead of `${{github.workspace}}/examples/resources/third_party/*`). This means CI has been passing without Sedna installed for every open PR. Combined with Bug 9, this means the PyPI name collision has been silently present in the project while CI reported green - a double failure that has made this the hardest class of bug to detect. --- ### **Bug 10 - KubeEdge Sedna has no pip-installable package structure** Even attempting to install from the official repo fails: ``` ERROR: git+https://github.com/kubeedge/sedna.git does not appear to be a Python project: neither 'setup.py' nor 'pyproject.toml' found. ``` > The only working installation path is completely undocumented: manual `git clone` + `export PYTHONPATH=~/kubeedge-sedna/lib:$PYTHONPATH`. **10 core Ianvs files** import from `sedna` - all 10 fail silently with the wrong package installed. The specific files are: `core/testcasecontroller/algorithm/paradigm/singletask_learning/singletask_learning.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/algorithm/paradigm/incremental_learning/incremental_learning.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/algorithm/paradigm/lifelong_learning/lifelong_learning.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/algorithm/paradigm/federated_learning/federated_learning.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/algorithm/paradigm/multiedge_inference/multiedge_inference.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/algorithm/paradigm/joint_inference/joint_inference.py`, `core/testenvmanager/dataset/dataset.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/testcase.py`, `core/testcasecontroller/testcasecontroller.py`, and `core/storymanager/story/story.py`. #### Motivation This is the highest-impact bug in the entire Ianvs ecosystem. Every contributor who follows any Ianvs documentation produces a silently broken environment, runs into confusing errors downstream, and has no systematic way to diagnose the root cause. The fix within Ianvs scope is threefold: add `colorlog` to core `requirements.txt`, document the correct manual Sedna installation procedure in the core README, and add a setup verification script that checks which sedna is installed. #### Pull Requests - [#315](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pulls/315) - fixes typos in requirements files but does not add `colorlog` or resolve the Sedna installation issue. - [#421](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pull/421) - adds `colorlog>=4.7.2` to core `requirements.txt`, directly fixes Bug 8 - [#414](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pull/414) - adds `colorlog` unpinned, same fix as #421 with alphabetical sorting - [#417](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pull/417) - fixes the broken CI path that was preventing Sedna from being installed in CI at all --- ## Issue [#353](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/353) - Government singletask: JSONMetaDataParse schema incompatibility **Category:** Sedna Core Bug - affects all LLM examples #### Introduction Issue #353 tracks a related but distinct problem in the government singletaskexample: `JSONMetaDataParse` silently drops fields beyond a basic `(x, y)`tuple, specifically the `options`, `prompt`, `judge_prompt`, and `dimension`metadata fields required for subjective evaluation. The smart_coding bugs documented below - Bugs 11 through 18 are a**separate and currently untracked set of failures** in `JsonlDataParse`,the parser smart_coding depends on. None of these bugs appear in any openGitHub issue. They were discovered through direct execution on a cleanenvironment and are reported here for the first time. The architectural root cause connecting both #353 and the smart_coding bugsis the same: Sedna's LLM data parsers (`JsonlDataParse` and`JSONMetaDataParse`) were written for one specific dataset schema and cannotserve other LLM examples without modification. For smart-coding specifically, the investigation uncovered four additional bugs in the only available `JsonlDataParse` implementation (a specific commit on a personal fork, never merged upstream): ### **Bug 11 - `JsonlDataParse` missing from official `kubeedge/sedna`** Official Sedna exports only: `BaseDataSource`, `TxtDataParse`, `CSVDataParse`, `JSONDataParse`. After manually installing KubeEdge Sedna: ``` ImportError: cannot import name 'JsonlDataParse' from 'sedna.datasources' ``` The IcyFeather fork's main branch also doesn't have it - it exists only at one specific SHA. The only path: `curl` a raw file from that commit directly. > --- ### **Bug 15 - `JsonlDataParse.parse()` missing `import json`** Even after getting the patched file, it immediately crashes: ``` File "sedna/datasources/__init__.py", line 238, in parse line = json.loads(line) NameError: name 'json' is not defined. Did you forget to import 'json'? ``` > --- ### **Bug 16 - `JsonlDataParse` hardcodes `'question'` but smart-coding schema uses `'query'`** ``` File "sedna/datasources/__init__.py", line 240, in parse x_data.append(line['question']) KeyError: 'question' ``` --- ### **Bug 17 - `JsonlDataParse` hardcodes `'answer'` but smart-coding schema uses `'response'`** ``` File "sedna/datasources/__init__.py", line 241, in parse y_data.append(line['answer']) KeyError: 'answer' ``` > --- ### **Bug 18 - `JSONMetaDataParse` constructs data path via fragile string replacement** ```python data_f = f.replace('metadata.json', 'data.jsonl') # line 277 ``` PR #429 attempts to fix this by injecting a new `JsonlDataParse` into `core/testenvmanager/dataset/dataset.py`. It hardcodes `raw_data.get("question", "")` as the field extractor. Smart-coding's JSONL uses `"query"` not `"question"`. With PR #429 merged, smart-coding silently loads 1000 empty strings into `self.x` with no error raised. The model runs inference on blank inputs for 25+ seconds per question. The benchmark completes and records a score. The leaderboard shows a number. No error is raised at any point. This is worse than a crash because a researcher sees a result and believes it. ## Motivation `JsonlDataParse` is positioned as a reusable Sedna core component for all LLM examples. With hardcoded field names tied to the government example's private dataset schema, it cannot serve any other LLM example. The parser was written for one specific dataset and incorrectly reused without adaptation. The correct fix is configurable field names - a single change that unblocks smart-coding, government, government_rag, and prevents the same failure in all future additions:: ```python class JsonlDataParse(BaseDataSource, ABC): def __init__(self, data_type, func=None, query_field='query', response_field='response'): super().__init__(data_type=data_type, func=func) self.query_field = query_field self.response_field = response_field def parse(self, *args, **kwargs): import json import numpy as np x_data, y_data = [], [] for f in args: if not (f and FileOps.exists(f)): continue with open(f, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file: for line in file: line = json.loads(line) x_data.append(line[self.query_field]) y_data.append(line[self.response_field]) self.x = np.array(x_data) self.y = np.array(y_data) ``` This single change unblocks smart-coding, government, government_rag, and all future LLM examples. The fix belongs in the Ianvs-bundled Sedna resources (`examples/resources/sedna-llm.zip`) since upstreaming to the official Sedna repo is outside Ianvs mentorship scope. ## Pull Requests - [#426](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pulls/426) - restores `government/singletask_learning_bench` and addresses some Sedna API issues; does not fix the field-name configurability problem that blocks smart-coding specifically. - [#429](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pull/429) - attempts to fix the pipeline but introduces the silent data corruption described above; do not merge as-is --- ## Issue [#194](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/194) - Track of Runnable Examples **Category:** Tracking #### Introduction The runnable examples tracker lists `smart_coding/smart_coding_learning_bench` as unverified/broken. This investigation confirms it with 19 documented bugs. Both sub-examples (`issue/` and `comment/`) are non-runnable on any fresh environment. ### Challenge The tracker shows 13/33 examples as runnable. Smart-coding contributes two sub-examples to the unrunnable count. The cross-cutting nature of the Sedna installation bugs (Bugs 9, 10, 11) means smart-coding cannot be made runnable by example-level fixes alone - it requires the ecosystem-level fixes in [#132](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/132) first. ### Motivation Smart-coding's broken state signals to new contributors that the v0.3.0 LLM benchmarking capabilities are unreliable, discouraging adoption for code-domain edge AI evaluation. Restoring it contributes three systemic fixes to Phase III: a documented Sedna installation path benefiting all examples, a corrected `JsonlDataParse`/`JSONMetaDataParse` unblocking the entire LLM family, and a reference `BaseModel` interface with `preprocess()` for all future LLM example contributors. ### Pull Requests - [#315](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pulls/315) - cleanup only, does not restore runnability. --- ## Issue [#230](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/230) - Comprehensive Example Restoration (Umbrella) **Category:** Umbrella / Systemic ### Introduction Issue #230 coordinates Phase III restoration across all Ianvs examples. Smart-coding's bugs, particularly the Sedna installation chain - are cross-cutting and block restoration of every LLM example simultaneously. All three root causes identified in #230 (dependency drift, missing CI, documentation misalignment) are present in smart-coding. ### Challenge The Sedna installation problem crosses project boundaries. Within Ianvs scope, the fix is: document the manual installation procedure, bundle the corrected Sedna datasources in `examples/resources/sedna-llm.zip`, and add a setup verification script. This is achievable without requiring changes to the upstream `kubeedge/sedna` repository. The dependency drift problem is compounded by the fact that CI was silently broken (PR #417 finding), meaning dependency regressions have been merging undetected. ### Motivation Issue #230 sets the standard for what a complete restoration looks like. A PR that only patches the most visible bugs without addressing the underlying Sedna installation gap or CI breakage does not meet that standard. Resolving smart-coding contributes three systemic fixes to Phase III: a documented Sedna installation path benefiting all examples, a corrected `JsonlDataParse`/`JSONMetaDataParse` unblocking the entire LLM family, and a reference `BaseModel` interface with `preprocess()` for all future LLM example contributors. ### Pull Requests - [#315](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pulls/315), [#426](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pulls/426) - partial contributions. - [#417](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/pull/417) - fixes the CI breakage that allowed ecosystem failures to go undetected --- ## Issue [#199](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/199) - Agent Benchmark for Government Scenarios (Design Context) **Category:** Design Origin ### Introduction Filed by IcyFeather233, the original smart-coding author. It proposes extending the domain-specific LLM benchmark family. This context explains why `JsonlDataParse` has hardcoded government-schema field names: it was designed for the government example's private dataset and reused for smart-coding without adaptation. ### Motivation IcyFeather233's ongoing work in #199 will create more LLM examples that depend on the same `JsonlDataParse`. The configurable field-name fix must happen before those examples are added, or Bugs 16 and 17 will repeat for every new LLM example added to the family. This makes the fix not just a smart-coding restoration — it is a prerequisite for healthy future LLM example development. ### Pull Requests None directly linked. --- ## Issue [#177](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/177) - Domain-specific LLM benchmarks: the edge perspective **Category:** Design Context #### Introduction Issue #177 proposes the broader framework for domain-specific LLM evaluation on edge devices, of which smart-coding is a concrete implementation. It establishes the design rationale for why a code-domain benchmark at the edge is distinct from general-purpose LLM evaluation. #### Motivation The bugs found in smart-coding - particularly the lack of CPU/MPS fallback (Bug 3) and the absence of any requirements specification (Bug 1) - are direct violations of the edge-deployment principles outlined in this issue. The vLLM fail-early CUDA guard pattern in PR #316 must explicitly not be applied to smart-coding, since Qwen2.5-Coder runs correctly on MPS and CPU. --- ## Issue [#96](https://github.com/kubeedge/ianvs/issues/96) - Cloud-edge collaborative inference for LLM (design origin) **Category:** Design Context #### Introduction Issue #96 is the foundational design issue for the cloud-edge LLM inference architecture that smart-coding's `singletasklearning` paradigm builds upon. Typos: Wrong spelling of **classification**, leading to failed executions of the above commands.

Python lib conflicts for an empty python venv:
- `numpy` should be installed manually before `running pip install -r requirements.txt`, since the later on `pytoomacoustic` package installation will throw errors about absence of `numpy` package.
- `acoular` requires `numba` and `numba` requires `numpy` version > 1.22. The current `numpy` version in the `requirements.txt` is 1.18, which is outdated. Verified that `numpy` 1.22 also works for the project.
